name: C-peptide
rangeNote: No default range: C-peptide has to be read with the blood glucose at the time of the sample, and labs and assays use different limits. The sample may be taken fasting or after a meal or stimulation test, and the setting changes the expected value. C-peptide is cleared by the kidneys, so it can read higher when kidney function is low. ng/mL to pmol/L uses the molar mass of C-peptide (about 3,020 g/mol).
summary: C-peptide is released from the pancreas in equal amounts with insulin, so it shows how much insulin the body is making itself. It is excreted at a steadier rate than insulin and is not affected by insulin injections.

high.meaning: A high C-peptide means the pancreas is releasing a lot of insulin, which can happen when the body responds poorly to insulin (insulin resistance). It is read together with a blood glucose measured at the same time.
commonCauses: Insulin resistance, as in type 2 diabetes or obesity
Recent meal or a stimulation test

low.meaning: A low C-peptide means the pancreas is making little insulin of its own. A level below 0.2 nmol/L has been associated with type 1 diabetes, and C-peptide is used to help classify diabetes in people on insulin.
commonCauses: Type 1 diabetes or other loss of insulin-producing cells
Long-standing diabetes with reduced insulin production
Fasting or a very low-carbohydrate state

sources.title: The clinical utility of C-peptide measurement in the care of patients with diabetes
A Practical Review of C-Peptide Testing in Diabetes
